title: English Kindergarten Anxiety Ledger
oneLiner: Korean parents compare English-kindergarten cost, policy uncertainty, commute fatigue, and status pressure without drowning in mom-chat panic.
theme: 사교육 / 체면 - prestige anxiety, child readiness, and household affordability.

phaseA.label: Fun / Portfolio / Commercial
phaseA.targetUser: Korean parents of preschool children deciding whether to enroll, continue, switch, or resist English-kindergarten spending.
phaseA.keyUx: Parent builds a monthly ledger that weighs tuition, commute, child fatigue, sibling fairness, policy uncertainty, and status pressure, then produces a family conversation card.
requiredUiSections: Family pressure header with monthly tuition, child age, commute, and spouse stance
Cost stack for tuition, shuttle, books, uniforms, extra tutoring, and make-up classes
Policy uncertainty lane for age rules, official statistics, and school-plan risk
Mom-chat claim parking lot that separates evidence from fear
Family decision card with enroll, wait, switch, or cap-spend options
phaseA.spreadTrigger: Parents share the family decision card with spouses or grandparents because it reframes status pressure as a calm receipt.
phaseA.stitchPrompt: Build a production-grade web app prototype called "English Kindergarten Anxiety Ledger" for Korean parents comparing English-kindergarten cost, policy uncertainty, commute fatigue, and status pressure without drowning in mom-chat panic. The first screen must be a working family decision surface with a pressure header, cost stack, policy uncertainty lane, child fatigue check-in, sibling fairness calculator, mom-chat claim parking lot, and family decision card. Use realistic sample data: KRW 1,545,000 monthly tuition, 38-minute commute, shuttle fee, five-year-old child, sibling entering daycare, policy rumor flagged as unverified, and grandparent pressure note. Design direction: use the calm-consumer profile with reassuring step cards, warm neutral surfaces, gentle blue-green accents, and copy that lowers shame while keeping the decision concrete. Do not make a marketing landing page; the first screen must be the working app.
